title: Government and retirement schemes: EPF, PPF, NPS, SCSS and SSY
objectives: Describe the main government-backed savings and pension schemes.
Match each scheme to a client need.
body_md:
## Schemes at a glance (rates and limits change: verify)

| Scheme | Key features |
|---|---|
| **EPF** | Employee and employer contribute (12% each of basic wage); interest declared yearly; tax-free on qualifying withdrawal |
| **PPF** | **15-year** term, up to ₹1.5 lakh a year, rate set quarterly, **EEE** status under the old regime |
| **NPS** | Market-linked pension; tier I (restricted) and tier II; extra deduction under **80CCD(1B)**; part of the corpus must buy an **annuity** at exit |
| **SCSS** | Age **60 and above**, 5-year term, quarterly interest, ceiling of ₹30 lakh |
| **SSY** | For a **girl child**, deposits for 15 years, matures at 21 years, ceiling ₹1.5 lakh a year |
| **POMIS** | Monthly income scheme through the post office, 5 years |

## Matching

- Long-term tax-efficient debt: **PPF**, **EPF**.
- Retirement corpus with equity exposure: **NPS**.
- Safe income after 60: **SCSS**, annuities.
- Daughter's education or marriage: **SSY**.

## Cautions

- PPF and SCSS have **contribution limits** and **lock-ins**.
- NPS withdrawal and annuity rules have changed; check current PFRDA rules.
- Tax benefits depend on the **tax regime** the client chooses.

> **Exam tip:** PPF 15 years, SCSS age 60+, SSY girl child up to 21 years.
example: A 62-year-old retiree with ₹25 lakh wanting safe quarterly income can put it in SCSS, within the ₹30 lakh ceiling.
say: This scheme has a lock-in, so keep a separate emergency fund.
Rates change, so I will check the current rate before you commit.
never: PPF returns are fixed for the full 15 years.
NPS has no rules on withdrawal.
